notes: Cluster slot discipline, for whoever tests next on this namespace: poll the lock, never trust a hand-over message. My pass at 10:47Z was refused by a run that took the lock three minutes after I was told the namespace was free, and I lost 50 minutes before reading the lock again; a waiter that polls every 30 s is the fix, and INFRA-598's tester's advice to hold the lock across a whole piece of work (cluster.sh hold) is the other half.

A harness defect I found and gave to INFRA-598 rather than fixing here: a 20Gi Postgres volume fills during a typed r16 replay. The copy's postgres-0 went to CrashLoopBackOff with `FATAL: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.49": No space left on device`, and 15 of 17 typed documents could not be checked (`dial error: timeout`). Its implementer has shipped --pg-volume (100Gi by default) and a step that stops under 15% free, and measured 9.4 GiB peak for that replay on 20Gi.

I cut pass A's whole-database stored-order check after 80 minutes (it is bounded at 7,200 s by default) and bounded it at 900 s for pass B. The acceptance is judged on the typed documents; the whole-database pass is extra coverage, and at this scale it costs more than the round can spend.
